summary: Data analyst who started as a theater electrician and now turns crew schedules, ticketing exports, and device logs into decisions operations teams can use. Eight years across live production and product analytics, with a habit of replacing shared spreadsheets with checks people actually trust.

education.institution: University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee, Peck School of the Arts
education.degree: Bachelor of Fine Arts, Theatre Production (Lighting)

projects.name: Cue Ledger
projects.subtitle: Python, SQLite
bullets: Built a desktop log for focus notes and channel changes during tech, used by the electrics crew on two Northline tours.
Exported a CSV the production manager could diff against the designer's paperwork, catching 12 mis-patched conventions before a 2020 opening.

projects.name: House Power Map
projects.subtitle: Observable, GeoJSON
bullets: Mapped circuit capacity for 11 small venues a civic arts fund supported, so visiting companies could see available dimmers before they advanced the show.
Published the map as a static page; three venues adopted it as the first sheet of their tech packet.

projects.name: Renewal Risk Notes
projects.subtitle: SQL, dbt, Looker
bullets: Scored Fieldnote accounts whose loggers had more than two unexplained outages in 90 days, separating battery faults from gateway dropouts.
Support used the list to schedule proactive swaps; the pilot cohort cut emergency shipments 15% over one quarter.

work_experience.title: Product Analyst
bullets: Own the weekly reliability review for a fleet of 1,200 portable environmental loggers used by municipal parks departments.
Built a dbt model in Snowflake that cut false 'sensor offline' alarms 37% by splitting battery faults from gateway dropouts.
Wrote acceptance criteria with firmware and support for a self-serve calibration flow, reducing related tickets 22% across two quarters.
Designed a Looker dashboard for account managers covering device uptime, replacement lead time, and sites at risk before renewal.

work_experience.title: Data Analyst
bullets: Modeled attendance and staffing for 14 neighborhood arts venues, replacing a spreadsheet three program managers updated by hand.
Wrote Python jobs that reconciled Spektrix ticketing exports with volunteer shift logs, closing a 6–9% attendance gap that had been booked as walk-up traffic.
Presented quarterly findings to a board committee; two venues moved from Thursday double-shifts to staggered calls and saved about 180 crew hours a season.

work_experience.title: Production Data Coordinator
bullets: Kept the advance packet and labor calendar for a 9-city contemporary dance tour, tracking 40+ local crew calls a week.
Replaced paper dimmer schedules with an Airtable base and a Python check that flagged conflicts between truck loads and venue power limits.
Cut load-in overtime at three venues by rewriting the cable pull order from the prior year's actuals instead of the design plot alone.

work_experience.title: Lighting Electrician
bullets: Hung, circuited, and focused repertory plots for a four-show season in the Quadracci Powerhouse, typically 180–220 instruments per turn.
Maintained the fixture and gel inventory designers used to decide rentals, reducing unplanned rental spend by about $4,000 in the 2017–18 season.
Trained 8 overhire electricians on the house console and safety checks before tech week.

leadership.title: Workshop Lead
bullets: Ran monthly skills nights for 15–25 early-career technicians covering knot craft, power distribution, and how to read a light plot.
Paired 30 participants with overhire calls at local houses over four seasons and kept a shared contact list houses still use.

personal_interests: Still calls the occasional community-theater show
Cross-country skiing on the Oak Leaf Trail
